title: Spin and the formation of the solar system

cards.back: $L = I\omega$. $I$ is the moment of inertia; $\omega$ is the spin rate in degrees per second (°/sec).
$I = mr^2$, in kg·m². The resistance to changing spin rate. Mass far from the spin axis counts much more ($r$ is squared). Two masses: add $mr^2$ for each.

$I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$. Ex. Two 5 kg balls move from 4 m to 6 m from the axis, spinning at 30°/sec. $I_1 = 2(5)(4)^2 = 160$, $I_2 = 2(5)(6)^2 = 360$, $\omega_2 = \dfrac{(160)(30)}{360} = 13.3$°/sec.

cards.back: Inward $F_{\rm gravity}$ = outward pressure from heat. Kids and teachers: the hot atoms (the kids) bounce around and push out; gravity (the teachers) pulls everyone back together.
A huge, cold cloud of mostly hydrogen gas and dust. The solar system began as one, 4.56 Gyr ago.

cards.front: Formation of the Solar System (nebular hypothesis)
cards.back: 1. A slowly spinning cloud radiates energy away and cools. 2. Pressure drops, gravity wins, the cloud shrinks. 3. Smaller $I$ means faster spin, and it flattens into a protoplanetary disk. 4. The center gets hot enough for fusion: the Sun. 5. Dust in the disk clumps into planetesimals, then planets, all orbiting the same way.
The flat, spinning disk of gas and dust around a newborn star, where planets form. ALMA has photographed them, for example around HL Tauri.

questions.explain: $L = I\omega$: moment of inertia times spin rate. $I = mr^2$ is the moment of inertia itself.

questions.stem: A {m} kg ball on a string swings in a circle of radius {r} m. What is its moment of inertia?
A merry-go-round turns once every {T} s. What is its spin rate $\omega$, in degrees per second?
A {m} kg ball on a {r} m string goes around once every {T} s. What is its angular momentum, using $\omega$ in °/sec?
Two 3 kg balls on a very light rod spin at {w}°/sec, each {a} m from the axis. They slide out to {b} m. What is the new spin rate?
questions.explain: $I_1 = 2(3)({a})^2$, $I_2 = 2(3)({b})^2$. $I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$ gives $\omega_2 = \dfrac{I_1\omega_1}{I_2} =$ {answer} °/sec. Farther out, slower spin.

questions.stem: A skater spins at {w}°/sec with arms out ($I_1 = {I}$ kg·m²). She pulls her arms in, so $I_2 = {J}$ kg·m². What is her new spin rate?
Why does a spinning skater speed up when she pulls her arms in?
choices: She pushes off the ice harder
Her moment of inertia drops, and since $L$ is conserved, $\omega$ goes up
questions.explain: $I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$. Bringing mass close to the axis makes $I = mr^2$ smaller, so $\omega$ must grow to keep $L$ the same.

questions.stem: Hydrostatic Equilibrium is a balance between
choices: the inward pull of gravity and the outward pressure from heat
the Sun's light and the planets' orbits
questions.explain: Inward $F_{\rm gravity}$ = outward pressure from heat: the teachers pulling in, the kids pushing out.

questions.stem: A cloud in Hydrostatic Equilibrium slowly radiates its energy away. What happens?
choices: Its pressure drops, gravity wins, and it shrinks
questions.explain: Losing energy cools the gas, so the outward pressure drops. Gravity is now stronger and the cloud contracts.

questions.stem: As a slowly spinning cloud shrinks, its spin rate
questions.explain: Smaller $r$ makes $I = mr^2$ smaller; $I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$ means $\omega$ goes up. Big with little spin becomes small with lots of spin.

questions.stem: A spinning cloud shrinks to 1/{k} of its radius. Treating it like $I = mr^2$, its spin rate becomes how many times as fast?
questions.explain: Relative form: $I$ becomes $\left(\frac{1}{{k}}\right)^2$ as big, so $\omega$ becomes $({k})^2 =$ {answer} times as fast.

questions.stem: Why is the solar system shaped like a flat disk rather than a ball?
choices: Gravity is stronger in one direction
As the spinning cloud shrank, it spun faster and flattened into a disk
The planets were pushed flat by sunlight
questions.explain: Gas can fall in freely along the spin axis, but in the midplane its spin keeps it out. The cloud collapses into a spinning protoplanetary disk, and the planets formed in it.

questions.stem: Put the formation of the solar system in order.
items: A slowly spinning giant molecular cloud
The cloud cools and gravity wins
It shrinks, spins faster and flattens into a protoplanetary disk
Fusion starts at the center: the Sun
questions.explain: Cloud, cooling, collapse and spin-up into a disk, the Sun lights up, then clumps grow into planets, all orbiting the same way the cloud spun.

questions.stem: All eight planets orbit the Sun in the same direction, in nearly the same plane. This tells us they
choices: formed at different times and were captured
formed from one spinning cloud of gas and dust
were thrown out of the Sun
questions.explain: They inherited the spin of the cloud and the flatness of its disk.
